_comment: INDUSTRIAL: a shore-connection manifold - a dark spine box down +Z with three capped sockets standing out of it. Ships get built plugged in, and a row of blanked umbilical points is what stays on the hull after the yard lets go: every one has a part number and a torque figure. Sockets are six-sided so the collars read as machined fittings rather than drums at hull distance. NO yellow - caps are shadow, collars are steel; the accent stays on edges, collars-of-paint and handles, and a socket collar is metal, not paint. Long axis is +Z so `align: Run` rows the sockets down the flank the way a gantry would have reached them.
